title: MakeMyTrip Launches 350 Guided Tours Across India With Tourism Ministry
excerpt: The collaboration offers curated experiences led by local experts across more than 60 Indian cities, bookable on the platform starting August 15.
body:
• MakeMyTrip and India's Ministry of Tourism have launched over 350 guided tours covering more than 60 cities nationwide.
  • The tours, led by local experts, aim to showcase India's heritage, culture, and lesser-known destinations.
  • Bookings went live on August 15, India's Independence Day, through the MakeMyTrip platform.
  • The initiative builds on MakeMyTrip's recent expansion into experiences, including its acquisition of tour operator Flamingo Transworld earlier this year.

A New Way to Explore India

MakeMyTrip has partnered with India's Ministry of Tourism to launch over 350 guided tours across the country, the companies announced on Thursday. The tours, covering more than 60 cities, became bookable on the MakeMyTrip platform starting August 15, coinciding with India's 80th Independence Day.

Local experts will lead the curated experiences, which aim to showcase India's diverse heritage and cultural destinations. The initiative reflects a broader push by both the government and private sector to boost domestic tourism and encourage travelers to explore the country's lesser-known destinations.

Building on an Experiences Push

The partnership comes on the heels of MakeMyTrip's aggressive expansion into the experiences segment. In July 2025, the company launched a global Tours & Attractions booking platform offering more than 200,000 activities across 1,100 cities in 130 countries.

"Experiences account for a significant share of spending when Indians travel overseas, yet discovering and booking them remains one of the most fragmented aspects of the journey."

— Rajesh Magow, MakeMyTrip Co-founder and Group CEO

In March 2026, MakeMyTrip acquired a majority stake in Flamingo Transworld, a regional tour operator, to strengthen its holiday packages business. The company also partnered with OpenAI in February 2026 to integrate AI-driven travel discovery through its Myra assistant, according to IBEF.

Government's Tourism Campaign

The Ministry of Tourism has previously collaborated with MakeMyTrip on the "Traveller's Map of India" microsite, which highlighted over 600 unconventional destinations as part of the government's "Dekho Apna Desh" campaign encouraging domestic tourism. The latest guided tours initiative deepens that partnership by offering bookable, expert-led experiences rather than destination recommendations alone.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For members of the Indian diaspora planning trips to India, the guided tours offer a convenient way to explore destinations beyond familiar circuits like Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur. With tours bookable in Indian rupees on a single platform, NRIs can plan cultural, heritage, and adventure experiences alongside their flights and hotel reservations.

The timing is strategic. India's outbound and inbound travel market has been growing steadily, with MakeMyTrip reporting $268.8 million in quarterly revenue and $2.61 billion in gross bookings during its most recent fiscal quarter, according to PhocusWire. The company's push into curated domestic experiences positions it to capture growing demand from both domestic travelers and diaspora visitors returning for extended trips.
